Fifty RA patients were prospectively recruited from the Biologic Therapy Unit of our hospital. Inclusion criteria were being in treatment with s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents and having had neither changes in therapy nor local corticosteroid injections in the previous 3 months. Patients underwent clinical, laboratory [28-joint DAS (DAS28) and Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI (simplified disease activity index))]and US (ultrasound) assessment at two time points, i.e. at peak plasma drug concentration and at trough plasma drug concentration. US (ultrasound) assessments were performed blindly to the anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agent, the administration time and the clinical and laboratory data. Twenty-eight joints were investigated for the presence and grade (0-3) of B-mode synovitis and synovial power Doppler signal. Global indices for B-mode synovitis (BSI) and Doppler synovitis (DSI) were calculated for 12 joints and for wrist-hand-ankle-foot joints. B-mode US (ultrasound) remission was defined as a BSI<1 and Doppler US (ultrasound) remission as a DSI<1.

In all, 129 lung cancer patients entered into the study. Of these data for 82 patients were complete (at baseline and follow-up). 57% of patients were of lower socioeconomic status and they had more health problems, less functioning, and more symptoms as compared to affluent patients. Of these, physical mobility (P = 0.05), energy (P = 0.01), role functioning (P = 0.04), physical functioning (P = 0.03), and breathlessness (P = 0.02) were significant at baseline. However, at follow-up assessment there was no significant difference between patient groups nor did any consistent pattern emerge.
results.reference: The present study, which is based on internationally accepted assessment tools for SLE patients, shows a significant relationship between increased disease activity and reduced physical function. This result emphasizes the importance of optimizing treatment aiming at reducing disease activity.

results.question: PSA repeatedly fluctuating levels are reassuring enough to avoid biopsy?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that patients with fluctuating PSA levels (flu-PSA) do not have a significantly different cancer detection rate compared to those with steadily increasing PSA levels (si-PSA). Therefore, fluctuating PSA levels are not reassuring enough to avoid biopsy, as cancer can still be detected in these patients.

no
contexts: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate specific antigen)) levels can show wide fluctuations when repeatedly measured. Here we investigatewd if: (a) biopsy timing influences the prostate cancer (PC (prostate cancer)) detection rate in patients with fluctuating PSA (flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen)) in comparison with patients with steadily increasing PSA (si-PSA (prostate specific antigen)); (b) PSA (prostate specific antigen) slope estimated in patients with flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen) predicts a different risk of cancer detection; (c) flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen) and si-PSA (prostate specific antigen) patients develop PC (prostate cancer) in topographically different sites; (d) the behaviour of pre-operative PSA (prostate specific antigen) is an expression of a disease with defferent characteristics to the following radical prostatectomy.

The study involved 211 patients who underwent at least a second biopsy after a first negative prostate biopsy. PSA (prostate specific antigen) Slope, PSA (prostate specific antigen) velocity (PSAV) and PSA (prostate specific antigen) doubling time (PSADT) were estimated. Flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen) level was defined as a PSA (prostate specific antigen) series with at least one PSA (prostate specific antigen) value lower than the one immediately preceding it.

82 patients had flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen) levels and 129 si-PSA (prostate specific antigen) levels. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of cancer detection, clinical or pathological stage, but the si-PSA (prostate specific antigen) group with cancer had a higher Gleason score. No difference was found for PSA (prostate specific antigen) Slope between flu-PSA (prostate specific antigen) patients with cancer and those without.

To examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality)) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate specific antigen)), grade, and stage are the classic triad used to predict BCR after radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)). Multiple nomograms use these to predict risk of BCR. A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR. However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality).

Poorly differentiated PC (prostate cancer) tends to be more common in patients with elevated CRP (serum c-reactive protein) levels (15.5 vs. 9.5%, p = 0.08). Analogously, patients with a Gleason score ≥8 PC (prostate cancer) had significantly higher median CRP (serum c-reactive protein) levels than those with a Gleason score ≤7 PC (1.9 vs. 1.2 mg/l, p = 0.03). However, neither uni- nor multivariate analysis showed an association between the preoperative CRP (serum c-reactive protein) level and the presence of a locally advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastases or a positive surgical margin. Moreover, multivariate analysis relativized the association between an elevated CRP (serum c-reactive protein) level and poor tumor differentiation.
results.reference: Our study demonstrates no difference in PC detection rate at repeat biopsy between patients with flu or si-PSA levels. PSA Slope, PSAV and PSADT were not found helpful tools in cancer detection.

results.question: Is zero central line-associated bloodstream infection rate sustainable?
results.answer:
The provided studies show that adoption of standardized care practices, including bundles and checklists, led to a significant reduction of the CLABSI rate to zero for over 370 consecutive days and later maintained at zero for over 600 days in a NICU setting. This indicates that a zero CLABSI rate can be sustained for extended periods with ongoing training, surveillance, and vigilance.

yes
contexts: Adoption and implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care leads to reductions in central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) rates in the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit). The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center.

Adoption of standardized care practices, including bundles and checklists, was associated with a significant reduction of the CLABSI rate to zero for>370 consecutive days in our NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) in 2012. Overall, our CLABSI rates decreased from 4.1 per 1000 line days in 2009 (13 infections; 3163 line days) to 0.94 in 2013 (2 infections; 2115 line days), which represents a 77% reduction over a 5-year period. In the first quarter of 2013, there was a brief increase in CLABSI rate to 3.3 per 1000 line days; after a series of interventions, the CLABSI rate was maintained at zero for>600 days. Ongoing training, surveillance, and vigilance with catheter insertion and maintenance practices and improved documentation were identified as key drivers for success.

Infection control rate was 31% in retention and 59% in the removal group after initial surgical treatment, and 81% and 91% at latest followup, respectively. Retrospective chart review was performed to record patient demographics, including age, sex, cancer diagnosis, and indication for removal. results.reference: High-quality training, strict compliance with evidence-based guidelines, and thorough documentation is associated with significant reductions in CLABSIs. Mindful organizing may lead to a better understanding of what goes into a unit's ability to handle peak demands and sustain extraordinary performance in the long-term.

results.question: Is gastric electrical stimulation superior to standard pharmacologic therapy in improving GI symptoms, healthcare resources, and long-term health care benefits?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that patients with gastroparesis treated via gastric electrical stimulation (GES) showed more sustained improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms over 36 months compared to those treated with medical therapy. Additionally, GES patients had significantly improved healthcare resource usage and decreased costs at 24 and 36 months, with no deaths reported in the GES group versus deaths in the medical therapy group. These findings support the superiority of GES over standard pharmacologic therapy in improving GI symptoms, healthcare resources, and long-term benefits.

yes
contexts: To compare symptoms, healthcare resource utilization and costs in two groups of patients with the symptoms of GP (general practitioner): those treated via gastric electrical stimulation (GES) and those treated with traditional pharmacological agents in an intensive outpatient program (MED).

Severe upper gastrointestinal (GI (gastrointestinal)) motor disorders, including gastroparesis (GP (general practitioner)), can consume significant health care resources. Many patients are refractory to traditional drug therapy.

Gastrointestinal symptoms were significantly different from baseline (F = 3.03, P<0.017) with GP (general practitioner) patients treated via GES showing more sustained improvement over 36 months than those treated via MED. Healthcare resource usage, measured via the IDIOMS, significantly improved at 12, 24 and 36 month follow-up for GES patients (F = 10.49, P<0.001), compared with patients receiving medical therapy, who demonstrated further deterioration. GP (general practitioner) patients treated via GES also proved superior to medical therapy at 24 and 36 months with regard to decreased costs (F = 4.85, P<0.001). Within group comparisons indicated significantly reduced hospital days for both patient groups; however, no statistical differences were noted between groups in terms of hospital days. Three of nine patients in the MED group died primarily from i.v. access related problems; none of the GES patients died.

Both medical therapy and laparoscopic antireflux surgery have been shown to improve quality of life in gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Although patients with poor symptom control or side effects on medical therapy might be expected to have improved quality of life after surgery, our aim was to determine, for the first time, whether patients whose symptoms are well controlled on medical therapy but who decide to undergo surgery (patient preference) would experience improved quality of life.
A long-term comparison of patients with devices (n = 9) vs intensive medical therapy (n = 9).
results.reference: We conclude that GES is more effective in improving long-term GI symptoms and costs, and decreasing use of healthcare resources than intensive medical therapy, in this sample of patients with the symptoms of GP followed for 3 years. Certain patients with GP form a high-risk group in terms of costs, quality of life, morbidity and mortality.

results.question: Should pulp chamber pulpotomy be seen as a permanent treatment?
results.answer:
The context from abstracts [3] and [4] discusses pulpotomy treatment with follow-up periods of 12 to 24 months, showing an 82% survival rate without additional treatment. However, some treated teeth still required further intervention such as root canal treatment, indicating that pulpotomy may not always be a permanent solution. Therefore, pulpotomy should not be seen as a permanent treatment in all cases.

no
contexts: The sample was composed of 25 patients. Preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health were restored in most patients. Cyclical pamidronate therapy in a 2-year-old child with skeletal fragility resulted in remodelling of vertebral fractures and improvement in bone mineral density (BMD (bone mineral density)) at distal radial and spinal sites. The BMD (bone mineral density) at both sites decreased precipitously within 24 months of stopping treatment, raising the question as to whether bisphosphonates can be stopped in a growing child with skeletal fragility.
At 24 months, the survival rate without any complementary treatment was estimated to be 82%. Two of the 17 treated teeth required root canal treatment for pain control and one for prosthetic reasons.

Seventeen patients, aged 7-54 years (mean of 37.2 year), were treated by pulpotomy and filling with ProRoot MTA(®)  in premolar or molar teeth with vital pulps and without clinical evidence of irreversible pulpitis. The patients were then followed up for 12 to 24 months and the teeth then assessed by clinical and radiographic examination. Statistical analysis was performed with Kaplan-Meier survival probability statistics to estimate the survival of the treated teeth.

All patients (606 joints) had successful TMJ surgeries through the VMPA (vascular-guided multilayer preauricular approach). All incisions healed favorably with an uneventful recovery. No patient developed permanent weakness of the facial nerve or other severe complications.
results.reference: Under the conditions of this study, pulpotomy offered a viable alternative to root canal treatment for teeth with vital pulps in the short term. However, there is insufficient clinical evidence to consider this technique for the treatment of every permanent tooth. results.question: Does transverse apex coincide with coronal apex levels (regional or global) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis?
results.answer:
The data show that regional and global coronal apexes coincide at the same or nearly the same level in most curves, but the most rotated vertebral level (transverse apex) shows higher variability and does not consistently align with these apex levels. Therefore, the transverse apex does not reliably coincide with the coronal apex levels in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.

no
contexts: Thirty-three structural curves of 25 consecutive patients scheduled for surgery for thoracic or thoracolumbar scoliosis were analyzed with standing anteroposterior radiographs and computed tomography scans covering the curve apexes and pelvis. Thoracic and lumbar curves were evaluated separately for all Type II curves. Vertebral rotations were normalized by the rotation of the pelvis. The most rotated vertebral (or disc) levels (transverse apex) were compared with the regional and global apex levels (vertebra or disc) (coronal apexes) of the corresponding curves separately.
To identify the regional and global apexes of curves in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and to compare the levels of those with the most rotated vertebral levels on computed tomography scans.

Regional and global apexes were at the same level in 18 (54.5%) curves, and within half a level in another 15 (45.4%), and the regional apex was one level higher in two curves (95% confidence levels: -0.82, +0.88). Comparison of the most rotated levels with regional and global apex levels revealed a higher variability, extending up to two levels for the global apex (95% confidence levels: -1.19, +1.54 levels for the global and -1.0, +1.41 levels for the regional apexes).

The terminology regarding the terms and definitions had been arbitrary until being refined and standardized by the Scoliosis Research Society Working Group on Three-Dimensional Terminology of Spinal Deformity. Apical vertebra or disc is defined as the most laterally deviated vertebra or disc in a scoliosis curve, but the most rotated vertebra (or disc) has not been included in this terminology. One study suggested that the most rotated vertebral level was always located at the apex.
To analyze the changes in the curve extent, pattern and the fusion level in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) patients who undergo delayed surgery instead of early surgery.
results.reference: This study demonstrated that the regional or global apex of a given curve is the most rotated level in only a minority of the curves. The most rotated level may be as far as two levels from the global apex and one level from the regional apex.

results.question: Does the Child Health Computing System adequately identify children with cerebral palsy?
results.answer:
The Child Health Computing System (CHCS) missed 47% of children with cerebral palsy recorded on the Northern Ireland Cerebral Palsy Register, and many of these children had no computer record of any medical diagnosis. Additionally, some cases recorded on the CHCS were not confirmed to have cerebral palsy upon follow-up. This indicates that the CHCS does not adequately identify children with cerebral palsy.

no
contexts: This paper assesses the usefulness of the Child Health Computing System as a source of information about children with cerebral palsy.

A comparative survey of information held on the Child Health Computing System (CHCS) and the Northern Ireland Cerebral Palsy Register (NICPR (northern ireland cerebral palsy register)) in one Health and Social Services Board in Northern Ireland was carried out. The sample comprised children with cerebral palsy aged 5-9 years.

Of the 135 cases recorded on the NICPR (northern ireland cerebral palsy register), 47 per cent were not found on the CHCS; the majority of these children had no computer record of any medical diagnosis. Of the 82 cases recorded on the CHCS, 10 (12 per cent) were not found on the NICPR (northern ireland cerebral palsy register); five of these cases (6 per cent) were found on follow-up not to have CP.

The objectives were to identify prognostic factors for the survival of children with cerebellar astrocytoma, and to evaluate the reproducibility and prognostic value of histological sub-classification and grading.

We performed a prospective follow-up study of 678 women and their children sampled from the Danish National Birth Cohort based on maternal alcohol consumption during pregnancy. At 5 years of age, the children were tested with the Movement Assessment Battery for Children. Parental education, maternal IQ, prenatal maternal smoking, the child's age at testing, sex of child, and tester were considered core confounders, while the full model also controlled for prenatal maternal average alcohol intake, maternal age and prepregnancy body mass index, parity, home environment, postnatal parental smoking, health status, participation in organized sport, and indicators for hearing and vision impairment.
results.reference: Unless improvements are made in case ascertainment, case validation and recording activities, the evidence suggests that the CHCS will not be able to provide the same quality of information for needs assessment and surveillance of very low birthweight infants in relation to cerebral palsy as is provided by a specialist case register.

results.question: Are we seeing the effects of public awareness campaigns?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that public awareness campaigns have been implemented, such as the 2008 English public antibiotic campaigns and skin cancer awareness campaigns over the last 20 years. One study specifically aimed to determine the effect of the 2008 antibiotic campaigns, and another sought to establish whether skin cancer awareness campaigns affected melanoma presentation. This suggests that the effects of public awareness campaigns are being observed and studied.

yes
contexts: To determine the effect of the 2008 English public antibiotic campaigns.

The last 20 years has seen a marked improvement in skin cancer awareness campaigns. We sought to establish whether this has affected the presenting Breslow thickness of malignant melanoma in the South West.

English and Scottish (acting as controls) adults aged>or = 15 years were questioned face to face about their attitudes to and use of antibiotics, in January 2008 (1888) before and in January 2009 (1830) after the antibiotic campaigns.

A unique dataset with assembled information from public institutions and analyses based on ordinary least square and robust random effects models was carried out. Dependent variables were traffic fatality and severe injury rates per population and vehicle fleet. Independent variables were: (1) presence of new national traffic law; (2) police officers per population; (3) number of traffic tickets per police officer; and (4) interaction effect of number of traffic tickets per police officer with traffic law reform. Oil prices, alcohol consumption, proportion of male population 15-24 years old, unemployment, road infrastructure investment, years' effects and regions' effects represented control variables.

Health services often spend more on safety interventions than seems cost-effective. This study investigates whether the public value safety-related health care improvements more highly than the same improvements in contexts where the health care system is not responsible.
results.reference: The proportion of thin 0-1 mm melanomas presenting in South West England has significantly increased from 2003 to 2012. There is no significant change in the thick>4 mm melanomas. This may be a result of increased public awareness due to effective public health campaigns which has significant prognostic and financial implications.

results.question: Is breast cancer prognosis inherited?
results.answer:
The study found that daughters and sisters of a proband (mother or oldest sister) with poor breast cancer prognosis had a significantly higher 5-year breast cancer mortality compared to those with a proband with good prognosis, suggesting that prognosis may be influenced by inherited factors. This indicates a familial pattern in breast cancer outcomes beyond just the risk of developing the disease.

yes
contexts: We carried out a population-based cohort study in Sweden based on the nationwide Multi-Generation Register. Among all women with breast cancer diagnosed from 1961 to 2001, 2,787 mother-daughter pairs and 831 sister pairs with breast cancer were identified; we achieved complete follow-up and classified 5-year breast cancer-specific prognosis among proband (mother or oldest sister) into tertiles as poor, intermediary, or good. We used Kaplan-Meier estimates of survival proportions and Cox models to calculate relative risks of dying from breast cancer within 5 years depending on the proband's outcome.
A genetic component is well established in the etiology of breast cancer. It is not well known, however, whether genetic traits also influence prognostic features of the malignant phenotype.

Treatment delays in breast cancer are generally thought to affect prognosis but the impact on survival remains unclear. Indicators for breast cancer care include time to primary treatment. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether time to primary treatment (TPT (time to primary treatment)) in breast cancer impacts survival.

The 5-year survival proportion among daughters whose mothers died within 5 years was 87% compared to 91% if the mother was alive (p = 0.03). Among sisters, the corresponding proportions were 70% and 88%, respectively (p = 0.001). After adjustment for potential confounders, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor prognosis had a 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality compared to those of a proband with good prognosis (hazard ratio [HR], 1.6; 95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)], 1.2 to 2.2; p for trend 0.002). This association was slightly stronger among sisters (HR, 1.8; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.0 to 3.4) than among daughters (HR, 1.6; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.1 to 2.3).

Breast cancer is the most common malignancy afflicting women, and the most common cancer overall in Jordan. A woman's decision to go for screening is influenced by her social support network. This study aims to explore Jordanian men's individual and contextual perspectives on women's breast cancer and their own role in the breast health of the females within their families.
results.reference: Breast cancer prognosis of a woman predicts the survival in her first-degree relatives with breast cancer. Our novel findings suggest that breast cancer prognosis might be inherited.

results.question: Does nuchal translucency thickness in the first trimester predict GDM onset during pregnancy?
results.answer:
The study comparing nuchal translucency (NT) thickness between women who developed gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and those with physiological pregnancies found no significant difference in NT values (p = 0.585). no
contexts: This study was planned to evaluate whether increased nuchal translucency (NT (nuchal translucency)) thickness in the first trimester of gestation can be related to onset of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM (gestational diabetes mellitus)) during pregnancy.

NT (nuchal translucency) was mesured by a Fetal Medicine Foundation certificated operator; GDM (gestational diabetes mellitus) was diagnosed at 24-28 weeks of gestation following Carpenter and Coustan criteria. There was no significative difference (p = 0.585) between NT (nuchal translucency) values in the study (mean = 1.56) and control group (mean = 1.54).

ANOVA Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U-test have been used for the biometric characteristics comparison of nowadays fetal population with those three decades ago and to test the hypothesis about the existence of secular growth acceleration during fetal life. results.question: Are the arginine vasopressin V1a receptor microsatellites related to hypersexuality in children with a prepubertal and early adolescent bipolar disorder phenotype?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a study examining the transmission of AVPR1A microsatellite repeats in children with a prepubertal and early adolescent bipolar disorder phenotype, specifically hypothesizing preferential transmission to hypersexual and uninhibited people-seeking probands. The study included assessment of hypersexuality and uninhibited behavior and genotyping of AVPR1A repeats, suggesting a direct investigation of the relationship. Although the exact results are not detailed here, the objective and methods indicate a focus on this association, supporting a link between AVPR1A microsatellites and hypersexuality in this population.

yes
contexts: To examine family-based transmission of the number of 5' flanking arginine vasopressin V1a receptor (AVPR1A) microsatellites, which include [(GATA)(14)] and complex [(CT)(4)-TT-(CT)(8)-(GT)(24)]repeats, in probands with a prepubertal and early adolescent bipolar disorder phenotype (PEA-BP (blood pressure)). Preferential transmission of the number of AVPR1A microsatellite repeats to hypersexual and uninhibited people-seeking probands was hypothesized, based on reports from preclinical work in the literature.

Subjects (N = 247) were outpatients who participated in either the National Institute of Mental Health-funded Phenomenology and Course of Pediatric Bipolar Disorders study or the Treatment of Early Age Mania (TEAM (treatment of early age mania)) study. Both studies required that subjects have current DSM-IV bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed phase) and a Children's Global Assessment Scale (CGAS) score<or=60. All subjects had elation and/or grandiosity. Subjects in the Phenomenology study were obtained from 1995 to 1998 by consecutive new case ascertainment from designated pediatric and psychiatric facilities. Comprehensive assessment of the probands included separate Washington University in St. Louis Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (WASH-U-KSADS) interviews of parents about their children and of children about themselves. Microsatellite genotyping of the AVPR1A repeats was conducted using fluorescently labeled primers and detected by laser-induced fluorescence. Alleles were determined with the assistance of semi-automated allele-calling software. There were 32 complete, biological trios (28 informative families) for the GATA repeat and 34 complete, biological trios (30 informative families) for the complex repeat. Data were analyzed using case-control and family-based association methods.

To examine the representativeness of a randomized controlled trial (RCT (randomized controlled trial)) sample versus one obtained by consecutive new case ascertainment, for subjects with child bipolar I disorder.
To correlate the presence of viral co-infection with clinical phenotype in children admitted with acute respiratory infections (ARI (acute respiratory infections)).
results.reference: Preferential transmission of AVPR1A to hypersexual or uninhibited people-seeking probands was not supported.

results.question: Stage I non-small cell lung carcinoma: really an early stage?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that Stage I non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) is considered an early stage, as the studies focus on surgical treatment outcomes specifically for Stage I disease and analyze prognostic factors within this group. yes
contexts: We review our results on surgical treatment of patients with stage I non-small cell lung carcinoma and we attempted to clarify the prognostic significance of some surgical--pathologic variables.

The analysis is based on 122 of 143 previously untreated patients with NPC treated with radiation therapy at The University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center between 1983 and 1992. Fifty-nine (48%) patients had squamous cell carcinoma; 63 (52%) had lymphoepitheliomas, undifferentiated NPC or poorly differentiated carcinoma, NOS (UNPC (undifferentiated npc or poorly differentiated carcinoma, nos)). We identified 94,173 patients with small cell carcinoma of which 88,605 (94.1%) and 5,568 (5.9%) had pulmonary small cell carcinoma and EPSCC, respectively. Few studies have assessed whether the advantage chemotherapy has been shown to have in treating advanced non-small lung carcinoma in clinical trials is transferrable to normal health care activity. The objective of our study was to analyze prognostic factors related to survival and to see whether cytostatic treatment was an independent predictor.

results.question: Does Residency Selection Criteria Predict Performance in Orthopaedic Surgery Residency?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that preresidency selection factors such as USMLE scores, clerkship honors, letters of recommendation, and other criteria were examined for their association with objective and subjective measures of resident performance. Although the exact results are not detailed here, the study's purpose and methods suggest that these criteria were analyzed for predictive value. Therefore, the context supports that residency selection criteria can predict performance in orthopaedic surgery residency.

yes
contexts: More than 1000 candidates applied for orthopaedic residency positions in 2014, and the competition is intense; approximately one-third of the candidates failed to secure a position in the match. Charts of 60 orthopaedic residents from our institution were reviewed. The residency training sites saw slightly more children, women, blacks, and Medicare and Medicaid patients. This study investigated associations between the performance of dental students in each of the three components of the selection procedure [academic average, Undergraduate Medicine and Health Sciences Admission Test (UMAT (undergraduate medicine and health sciences admission test)) and structured interview], socio-demographic characteristics and their academic success in an undergraduate dental surgery programme.
results.reference: We found that USMLE Step 2, number of honors in medical school clerkships, and AOA membership demonstrated the strongest correlations with resident performance. results.question: Optimism and survival: does an optimistic outlook predict better survival at advanced ages?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that an optimistic outlook is associated with a lower risk of death among the oldest-old, particularly in women, even after adjusting for confounding factors such as physical and cognitive functioning and disease. Although the effect in men was weaker and not statistically significant after adjustment, the general pattern suggests optimism predicts better survival at advanced ages.

yes
contexts: Studies examining predictors of survival among the oldest-old have primarily focused on objective measures, such as physical function and health status. Only a few studies have examined the effect of personality traits on survival, such as optimism. The aim of this study was to examine whether an optimistic outlook predicts survival among the oldest-old.

During the follow-up period of 12 years (1998-2010) there were 2,239 deaths (99 %) in the 1905 Cohort Survey. Univariable analyses revealed that optimistic women and men were at lower risk of death compared to their neutral counterparts [HR 0.82, 95 % CI (0.73-0.93) and 0.81, 95 % CI (0.66-0.99), respectively]. When confounding factors such as baseline physical and cognitive functioning and disease were taken into account the association between optimism and survival weakened in both sexes, but the general pattern persisted. Optimistic women were still at lower risk of death compared to neutral women [HR 0.85, 95 % CI (0.74-0.97)]. The risk of death was also decreased for optimistic men compared to their neutral counterparts, but the effect was non-significant [HR 0.91, 95 % CI (0.73-1.13)].

There were no differences in background, such as preoperative pulmonary function, operation procedures, or operative mortality. The proportions of adenocarcinoma and pathologic stage I in women were greater than those in men (93.6% vs 61.7% and 71.4% vs 58.6%, respectively) (P<.001). Overall 5-year survival of women was better than that of men (81% vs 70%, P<.001). results.question: Are pectins involved in cold acclimation and de-acclimation of winter oil-seed rape plants?

results.question: Updating emotional content in working memory: a depression-specific deficit?

results.question: Does ultrasound imaging before puncture facilitate internal jugular vein cannulation?
results.answer:
The evidence shows that prepuncture ultrasound guidance does not significantly improve cannulation success or reduce complications in patients where respiratory jugular venodilation is identifiable. results.question: Should prostate specific antigen be adjusted for body mass index?
results.answer:

results.question: Does obstructive sleep apnea affect aerobic fitness?
results.answer:

results.question: Literacy after cerebral hemispherectomy: Can the isolated right hemisphere read?

results.question: Characterization of the gender dimorphism after injury and hemorrhagic shock: are hormonal differences responsible?
