Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (area under the curve [AUC (area under the curve)]) were compared to assess the predictive accuracy of the models for SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection). Pearson's chi-square was used to determine which models were able to risk-stratify patients into groups with significantly differing rates of actual SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection).

To examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality)) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate specific antigen)), grade, and stage are the classic triad used to predict BCR after radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)). Multiple nomograms use these to predict risk of BCR. A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR. However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality).

We found that each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR and PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality) in a statistically significant manner and that they all predicted PCSM (predict prostate cancer-specific mortality) more accurately than they predicted BCR (ie, with higher c-index values).
results.reference: All five existing predictive models have limited ability to risk-stratify patients and accurately assess risk of SSO. However, both the VHRS and ACS-NSQIP demonstrate modest success in identifying patients at risk for SSI. Continued model refinement is needed to improve the two highest performing models (VHRS and ACS-NSQIP) along with investigation to determine whether modifications to perioperative management based on risk stratification can improve outcomes.

results.question: Can EMS Providers Provide Appropriate Tidal Volumes in a Simulated Adult-sized Patient with a Pediatric-sized Bag-Valve-Mask?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that EMS providers using a pediatric BVM delivered lower median tidal volumes compared to an adult BVM in simulated scenarios, with volumes closer to lung-protective ventilation targets. Although the pediatric BVM provided lower volumes, it was sufficient to ventilate the patient simulator, and a greater percentage of breaths were within the recommended tidal volume range when using the pediatric BVM. Therefore, EMS providers can provide appropriate tidal volumes in a simulated adult-sized patient with a pediatric-sized BVM.

yes
contexts: We enrolled 50 providers from a large, busy, urban fire-based EMS agency with 14.96 (SD = 9.92) mean years of experience. Only 1.5% of all breaths delivered with the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) during the ventilation scenarios were below the recommended tidal volume. A greater percentage of breaths delivered in the recommended range occurred when the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) was used (17.5% vs 5.1%, p<0.001). Median volumes for each scenario were 570.5mL, 664.0mL, 663.0mL for the pediatric BMV and 796.0mL, 994.5mL, 981.5mL for the adult BVM (bag-valve-mask). In all three categories of airway devices, the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) provided lower median tidal volumes (p<0.001).

In the prehospital setting, Emergency Medical Services (EMS) professionals rely on providing positive pressure ventilation with a bag-valve-mask (BVM (bag-valve-mask)). Multiple emergency medicine and critical care studies have shown that lung-protective ventilation protocols reduce morbidity and mortality. Our primary objective was to determine if a group of EMS professionals could provide ventilations with a smaller BVM (bag-valve-mask) that would be sufficient to ventilate patients. Secondary objectives included 1) if the pediatric bag provided volumes similar to lung-protective ventilation in the hospital setting and 2) compare volumes provided to the patient depending on the type of airway (mask, King tube, and intubation).

Using a patient simulator of a head and thorax that was able to record respiratory rate, tidal volume, peak pressure, and minute volume via a laptop computer, participants were asked to ventilate the simulator during six 1-minute ventilation tests. The first scenario was BVM (bag-valve-mask) ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway in place ventilating with both an adult- and pediatric-sized BVM (bag-valve-mask), the second scenario had a supraglottic airway and both bags, and the third scenario had an endotracheal tube and both bags. Participants were enrolled in convenience manner while they were on-duty and the research staff was able to travel to their stations. Prior to enrolling, participants were not given any additional training on ventilation skills.

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.

An instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS was designed. Laypersons were handed a bag containing a LMAS, a bag mask valve device (BMV (bag mask valve device)), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed. Time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated.
results.reference: The study suggests that ventilating an adult patient is possible with a smaller, pediatric-sized BVM. The tidal volumes recorded with the pediatric BVM were more consistent with lung-protective ventilation volumes.

results.question: Can students' scores on preclerkship clinical performance examinations predict that they will fail a senior clinical performance examination?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that students' low performances on year 2 clinical performance examinations (CPEs) strongly predict failure on the senior CPE. Additionally, statistical analyses such as contingency tables and correlations support the predictive value of preclerkship CPE scores for senior CPE outcomes. Therefore, the evidence supports that preclerkship CPE scores can predict failure on the senior CPE.

yes
contexts: Students' low performances relative to their class on the year 2 CPEs were a strong predictor that they would fail the senior CPE (clinical performance examination). Their USMLE (united states medical licensing examination) Step 1 scores also correlated with their performance on the senior CPE (clinical performance examination), although the predictive values for these scores were considerably weaker.

This study was designed to determine whether preclerkship performance examinations could accurately identify medical students at risk for failing a senior clinical performance examination (CPE (clinical performance examination)).

This study used a retrospective case-control, multiyear design, with contingency table analyses, to examine the performance of 412 students in the classes of 2005 to 2010 at a midwestern medical school. During their second year, these students took four CPEs that each used three standardized patient (SP (standardized patient)) cases, for a total of 12 cases. The authors correlated each student's average year 2 case score with the student's average case score on a senior (year 4) CPE (clinical performance examination). Contingency table analysis was carried out using performance on the year 2 CPEs and passing/failing the senior CPE (clinical performance examination). Similar analyses using each student's United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE (united states medical licensing examination)) Step 1 scores were also performed. Sensitivity, specificity, odds ratio, and relative risk were calculated for two year 2 performance standards.

We tested the hypothesis that equal mastery of surgical clerkship objectives can be obtained in a clerkship with and without general surgery. Students chose any two surgical rotations and were assessed by written examination, objective structured clinical examination (OSCE (objective structured clinical examination)), ward evaluations, self-assessment objectives questionnaire, and satisfaction survey.

The score for overall performance at selection achieved statistically significant correlation  with examination performance (r = 0.491 for the AKT (applied knowledge test) and r = 0.526 for the CSA (clinical skills assessment), P<0.01).
results.reference: Under the conditions of this study, preclerkship (year 2) CPEs strongly predicted medical students at risk for failing a senior CPE. This finding opens the opportunity for remediation of deficits prior to or during clerkships.

results.question: Recovery Outcome Measures: Is There a Place for Culture, Attitudes, and Faith?
results.answer:
The first abstract indicates that the use of the Recovery Attitudes Questionnaire (RAQ) raised questions about the links between attitudes, faith, and culture in supporting the recovery journey, especially in secular multicultural societies. This suggests that culture, attitudes, and faith may play a role in recovery outcome measures. No other abstracts directly address this question.

yes
contexts: Utilization of the Recovery Knowledge Inventory (RKI (recovery knowledge inventory)) and Recovery Attitudes Questionnaire (RAQ (recovery attitudes questionnaire)) in southeastern Australia raised questions about the RAQ (recovery attitudes questionnaire), including links between attitudes, faith, and culture in supporting the recovery journey. These questions are particularly important when considered in the context of people with mental illness who live in secular multicultural societies.
Retrospective analysis of outcome measures.

In a retrospective review of 150 culture-positive and 150 culture-negative consecutively sampled tuberculosis (TB (tuberculosis)) suspects, treatment decisions were analysed at presentation, after the availability of culture detection results and after the availability of drug susceptibility testing (DST (drug susceptibility testing)) culture results.

Outcome measures included HbA1c (hemoglobin A1c), treatment failure, weight, hypoglycemic events and symptoms, satisfaction with treatment, general well-being, and fear of injecting insulin and testing.

Although there is evidence for the influential role of transformational leadership on health outcomes, researchers have used either attitude outcomes (e.g. job satisfaction) or softer health measures, such as general well-being. Specific measures of well-being such as sleep quality have not been used, despite its association with working conditions.
results.reference: This paper discusses the cultural appropriateness of the RAQ in Australian settings, and identifies the need to develop rigorous, inclusive recovery outcome measures.

results.question: Can surgeon familiarization with current evidence lead to a change in practice?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1] and [2] shows that mailing a summary of current evidence to surgeons led to a comparison of prophylactic nasogastric decompression use before and after the intervention. This implies that surgeon familiarization with current evidence can influence and change their practice to align more closely with evidence-based recommendations.

yes
contexts: Despite evidence against its utility, many surgeons continue to employ prophylactic nasogastric decompression in elective colonic resection. This study aimed to establish whether an easy and practical intervention, mailing out a summary of current evidence to surgeons, can change surgeons practice to bring it more in line with current evidence.

The use of prophylactic nasogastric (NG) decompression in elective colonic resections was documented for the 2 consecutive months of October and November, 2004 at the Royal Alexandra Hospital (RAH (royal alexandra hospital)). A one page summary of recent evidence concerning this practice was then mailed to all general surgeons at that institution. A similar second review was carried out for the months of January and February, 2005. The two periods were compared with regards to prophylactic NG use.

To determine current practice and to assess the value of routine follow-up procedures for endometrial cancer surveillance. To discuss whether such procedures are feasible and effective to identify asymptomatic recurrences and describe the pattern of relapse detected by procedures.

The "July effect" refers to the phenomenon of adverse impacts on patient care arising from the changeover in medical staff that takes place during this month at academic medical centres in North America. There has been some evidence supporting the presence of the July effect, including data from surgical specialties. Uniformity of care, regardless of time of year, is required for patients undergoing major cancer surgery. We therefore sought to perform a population-level assessment for the presence of a July effect in this field.

As with some procedures, trauma fellowship training and greater surgeon experience may result in better outcomes following intramedullary nailing (IMN) of diaphyseal femur fractures. However, surgeons with such training and experience may not always be available to all patients. The purpose of this study is to determine whether trauma training affects the post-operative difference in femoral version (DFV (difference in femoral version)) following IMN.
results.reference: This study has shown that mailing out a summary of current evidence to surgeons concerning a certain issue is not sufficient to lead to a change in practice.

results.question: Advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma in Thai women: should we continue to offer second-look laparotomy?
results.answer:
The study shows that patients who underwent second-look laparotomy (SLL) had a significantly lower five-year survival rate (37%) compared to those who refused the procedure (88%), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.001). Additionally, disease-free survival was not significantly better in the SLL group. These findings suggest that offering second-look laparotomy may not improve survival outcomes in advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma patients.

no
contexts: To determine survival among patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma)) who underwent a second-look laparotomy (SLL (second-look laparotomy)) and those refusing the procedure. Also to analyze factor(s) influencing the survival of the patients.

Medical records were reviewed of patients with advanced EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma) who were clinically free of disease after primary surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy between January 1, 1992, and December 31, 1998. All of them were offered SLL (second-look laparotomy). Measurement outcomes include patient survival and disease-free survival.

There were 50 patients with clinically complete remission after chemotherapy. Sixteen patients underwent SLL (second-look laparotomy), and thirty-four patients refused the procedure (NSLL). Seven patients (43.8%) were reported to have positive SLL (second-look laparotomy). After the median follow-up time of 35 months, 12 patients had died, and 5 patients were lost to follow-up. The median survival time for patients with SLL (second-look laparotomy) was about 60 months. Five-year survival rates of patients in the SLL (second-look laparotomy), and NSLL groups were 37 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 7%-69%), and 88 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 65%-96%) respectively (P<0.001). The median time to relapse was about 25 months for patients with negative SLL (second-look laparotomy). Five-year disease-free survival rates of patients in the negative SLL (second-look laparotomy), and NSLL groups were 28 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 4%-59%), and 54 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 34%-70%) respectively (P=0.251). By Cox regression analysis, tumor grade was the only significant prognostic factor influencing patients' survival (HR = 6, 95%CI (confidence interval) of HR = 1.2-34.2).
To evaluate surgical outcome and survival benefit after quaternary cytoreduction (QC (quaternary cytoreduction)) in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC (epithelial ovarian cancer)) relapse.

Surgical excision of ovarian endometriomas in patients desiring pregnancy has recently been criticized because of the risk of damage to healthy ovarian tissue and consequent reduction of ovarian reserve. A correct diagnosis in cases not scheduled for surgery is therefore mandatory in order to avoid unexpected ovarian cancer misdiagnosis. Endometriosis is often associated with high levels of CA125. This marker is therefore not useful for discriminating ovarian endometrioma from ovarian malignancy. The aim of this study was to establish if the serum marker CA72-4 could be helpful in the differential diagnosis between ovarian endometriosis and epithelial ovarian cancer.
results.reference: The second-look laparotomy doesn't have a favorable impact on overall and disease-free survival. Tumor grade is the only independent prognostic variable for survival of the patients.

results.question: Is high-sensitivity C-reactive protein associated with carotid atherosclerosis in healthy Koreans?
results.answer:
The first abstract specifically investigates the relationship between high-sensitivity CRP (hsCRP) levels and carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) in healthy Koreans, indicating a focus on the association between hsCRP and carotid atherosclerosis. However, it states that the association is controversial, implying that the evidence is not definitive. No other abstracts provide direct evidence to confirm or refute this association in healthy Koreans.

maybe
contexts: There is a positive association between chronic inflammation and the risk of cardiovascular disease, but whether there is an association between C-reactive protein (CRP (association between c-reactive protein)) and carotid atherosclerosis is controversial. We investigated the relationship between high-sensitivity CRP (hsCRP) levels and carotid intima-media thickness (IMT (carotid intima-media thickness)) in healthy Koreans.

The serum C-reactive protein (CRP (serum c-reactive protein)) level correlates with the clinical prognosis in patients with kidney, penile and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PC (prostate cancer)). We prospectively evaluated the preoperative CRP (serum c-reactive protein) level as a predictive marker for an advanced tumor stage or high-grade cancer in patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer).

Poorly differentiated PC (prostate cancer) tends to be more common in patients with elevated CRP (serum c-reactive protein) levels (15.5 vs. 9.5%, p = 0.08). Analogously, patients with a Gleason score ≥8 PC (prostate cancer) had significantly higher median CRP (serum c-reactive protein) levels than those with a Gleason score ≤7 PC (1.9 vs. 1.2 mg/l, p = 0.03). However, neither uni- nor multivariate analysis showed an association between the preoperative CRP (serum c-reactive protein) level and the presence of a locally advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastases or a positive surgical margin. CRP (serum c-reactive protein) also failed to correlate with the initial PSA (prostate specific antigen) level and the clinical tumor-associated findings. Moreover, multivariate analysis relativized the association between an elevated CRP (serum c-reactive protein) level and poor tumor differentiation.

Overall, 205 consecutive patients underwent preoperative carotid screening. The prevalence of significant carotid stenosis was 5.8%. Univariate analysis confirmed that PVD (P=0.005), carotid bruit (P=0.003) and diabetes mellitus (P=0.05) were significant risk factors for stenosis. Carotid stenosis was a risk factor for stroke (P=0.03). Prevalence of carotid stenosis was higher in the high-risk group (9.1%) than the low-risk group (1.2%) (P<0.05). All concomitant or staged carotid endarterectomies/CAB (5/205) and all patients who had perioperative strokes (5/205) were in the high-risk group (P=0.01).

Several prospective randomized trials have proved carotid endarterectomy to be safe and effective for both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients younger than 80 years of age. Recently, carotid artery stenting (CAS) has been approved for use in selected high-risk patients. It has been proposed that being an octogenarian places patients in this high-risk category.
results.reference: Both hsCRP levels and the carotid IMT were strongly correlated with conventional cardiovascular risk factors, but there was no independent association between hsCRP levels and carotid IMT in healthy Korean adults.

results.question: Validation of the 2009 TNM version in a large multi-institutional cohort of patients treated for renal cell carcinoma: are further improvements needed?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts mention the 2009 TNM staging system modifications for kidney cancers, including subclassifications of T2 and T3 stages, but do not provide data or analysis from a large multi-institutional cohort validating this system or discussing the need for further improvements. Therefore, there is no direct evidence in the context to support or refute whether further improvements are needed.

maybe
contexts: To determine whether there is a relationship between VEGF expression and renal vein and vena cava invasion in stage pT3 renal cell carcinoma and to evaluate the impact of VEGF expression on survival in pT3 renal cell carcinoma.

Patients enrolled in the study had been diagnosed with non-small cell carcinoma in stages IV or IIIB with pleural or N2-N3 involvement and with a performance status of 2 or below according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group)). Survival was analyzed with regard to the following variables: age, sex, comorbidity, weight loss, laboratory test results, histological type, ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group) score, TNM staging, and treatment. The Student t test, the chi(2) test, the Kaplan-Meier method, the log-rank test, and Cox regression analysis were used in the statistical analysis.

A new edition of the TNM was recently released that includes modifications for the staging system of kidney cancers. Specifically, T2 cancers were subclassified into T2a and T2b (<or =10 cm vs>10 cm), tumors with renal vein involvement or perinephric fat involvement were classified as T3a cancers, and those with adrenal involvement were classified as T4 (thyroxine) cancers.

The analysis is based on 122 of 143 previously untreated patients with NPC treated with radiation therapy at The University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center between 1983 and 1992. Excluded were 4 patients treated with palliative intent, 4 children, 12 patients not staged with CT (computerized tomography), and 1 patient who died of a cerebrovascular accident prior to completion of treatment. The stage distribution was as follows: AJCC Stage I-2, Stage II-7, Stage III-12, Stage IV-101; Tl-15, T2-33, T3 (triiodothyronine)-22, T4 (thyroxine)-52; N0-32, N1-10, N2-47, N3-32, Nx-1. Fifty-nine (48%) patients had squamous cell carcinoma; 63 (52%) had lymphoepitheliomas, undifferentiated NPC or poorly differentiated carcinoma, NOS (UNPC (undifferentiated npc or poorly differentiated carcinoma, nos)). Sixty-seven patients (65 with Stage IV disease) received induction chemotherapy. Fifty-eight patients (24 of whom had induction chemotherapy) were treated with the concomitant boost fractionation schedule. The median follow-up for surviving patients was 57 months.

Twenty-four patients operated on for stages T1 and T2 of the NSCLC (non small cell lung cancer), were enrolled in the study. Peripheral blood and LN tissue were obtained from different lymph node sites and levels. As a control, LN tissue was taken from patients diagnosed with emphysema or pneumothorax. The cells from randomly chosen LN were tested by multi-color flow cytometry. Separate portions of LN were snap-frozen and examined for the presence of cytokeratin positive cells (CK). Propensity for apoptosis, level of TCR zeta chain expression of T cells and the number and maturation status of dendritic cells were confronted with the presence of CK-positive cells.
results.reference: The recently released seventh edition of the primary tumor staging system for kidney tumors is a powerful predictor of CSS. However, some of the substages identified by the classification have overlapping prognoses, and other substages include patients with heterogeneous outcomes. The few modifications included in this edition may have not resolved the most critical issues in the previous version.

results.question: Are interstitial fluid concentrations of meropenem equivalent to plasma concentrations in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy?
results.answer:
The data show that interstitial fluid (ISF) concentrations of meropenem are lower than plasma concentrations in patients on continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration, with ISF penetration estimated at 63%-69% of plasma levels. This indicates that ISF concentrations are not equivalent but rather a fraction of plasma concentrations in this setting.

no
contexts: To describe the interstitial fluid (ISF) and plasma pharmacokinetics of meropenem in patients on continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF).

This was a prospective observational pharmacokinetic study. Meropenem (500 mg) was administered every 8 h. CVVHDF was targeted as a 2-3 L/h exchange using a polyacrylonitrile filter with a surface area of 1.05 m2 and a blood flow rate of 200 mL/min. Serial blood (pre- and post-filter), filtrate/dialysate and ISF concentrations were measured on 2 days of treatment (Profiles A and B). Subcutaneous tissue ISF concentrations were determined using microdialysis.

A total of 384 samples were collected. During Profile A, the comparative median (IQR) ISF and plasma peak concentrations were 13.6 (12.0-16.8) and 40.7 (36.6-45.6) mg/L and the trough concentrations were 2.6 (2.4-3.4) and 4.9 (3.5-5.0) mg/L, respectively. During Profile B, the ISF trough concentrations increased by ∼40%. Meropenem ISF penetration was estimated at 63% (60%-69%) and 69% (65%-74%) for Profiles A and B, respectively, using comparative plasma and ISF AUCs. For Profile A, the plasma elimination t1/2 was 3.7 (3.3-4.0) h, the volume of distribution was 0.35 (0.25-0.46) L/kg, the total clearance was 4.1 (4.1-4.8) L/h and the CVVHDF clearance was 2.9 (2.7-3.1) L/h.

Tacrolimus is a potent immunosuppressive drug used in organ transplantation. Because of its substantial toxic effects, narrow therapeutic index, and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability, therapeutic drug monitoring of whole-blood tacrolimus concentrations has been recommended. We investigated the comparability of the results of 2 immunoassay systems, affinity column-mediated immunoassay (ACMIA) and microparticle enzyme immunoassay (MEIA), comparing differences in the tacrolimus concentrations measured by the 2 methods in relation to the hematologic and biochemical values of hepatic and renal functions.

All three adducts were elevated in uremic plasma. Plasma CML (chronic myeloid leukemia) levels were mainly (>95%) albumin bound. Their levels were not correlated with fructoselysine levels and were similar in diabetic and non-diabetic patients on hemodialysis, indicating that their increase was not driven by glucose. Pentosidine and MDA-lysine were also increased in plasma to the same extent in diabetic and non-diabetic hemodialysis patients. Statistical analysis indicated that plasma levels of CML (chronic myeloid leukemia) correlated weakly (P<0.05) with those of pentosidine and MDA-lysine, but that pentosidine and MDA-lysine varied independently (P>0.5).
results.reference: This is the first known report of concurrent plasma and ISF concentrations of a meropenem antibiotic during CVVHDF. We observed that the ISF concentrations of meropenem were significantly lower than the plasma concentrations, although the present dose was appropriate for infections caused by intermediately susceptible pathogens (MIC≤4 mg/L).

results.question: Does Sensation Return to the Nasal Tip After Microfat Grafting?
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts shows that after microfat injections, patients initially experience decreased sensation in the nasal tip, but this sensation gradually recovers over time, with touch threshold values approaching preoperative levels by 12 weeks. Additionally, the percentage of patients experiencing paresthesia diminishes to none during the follow-up period, indicating that sensation does return.

yes
contexts: Patients usually complain about numbness in the nasal tip after microfat injections. The present study evaluated the severity of the numbness in the nasal tip after the procedure.

To address the research question, a prospective study of young women was designed and performed at the Beijing Anzhen Hospital. Time was the primary predictor variable. The nasal tip sensation, which was evaluated using objective and subjective assessments, was used as the primary outcome variable. The McNemar-Bowker test (time vs nasal tip sensation) was used to detect statistical significance.

A total of 30 young women (age 20.04 ± 3.63 years) were recruited for the present study. The preoperative mean touch threshold value was 3.60 units. One week after the injection, the women experienced a decrease in the touch threshold value by 2.50 units. However, the sensation recovered gradually during the follow-up period (1.51 units at week 2, 2.39 units at week 4, 3.01 units at week 8, and 3.35 units at week 12). Significant differences were detected between multiple different measurement points (P<.05). The percentage of those experiencing paresthesia after the microfat injections also gradually diminished to none.

Only patients with isolated nasal fractures were included in the study. Patients with additional maxillofacial fractures and patients whose application time to our clinic was more than 10 days after the trauma were excluded. Patients were classified into 5 types according to their fracture. All patients underwent closed reduction and external fixation under local anesthesia. Patients were asked about their satisfaction in a survey at 28th day and sixth month after the surgery. Patients were divided into groups according to fracture type and intervention time, and the results of the survey were evaluated.
To describe the biomechanical and wound healing characteristics of corneas after excimer laser keratorefractive surgery.
results.reference: Postoperative numbness occurs in most patients receiving nasal microfat injections. Partial to complete recovery of nasal tip sensation can be expected to occur over a 3-month period.

results.question: Do older men benefit from curative therapy of localized prostate cancer?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that older men with localized prostate cancer benefit from curative therapy depending on tumor differentiation and comorbidity status. Specifically, men with moderately or poorly differentiated tumors gain life expectancy and quality-adjusted life expectancy benefits up to ages 75-80, while those with well-differentiated tumors do not see QALE improvement. Benefits are limited to men with mild or no comorbidities.

yes
contexts: For men with well-differentiated tumors and few comorbidities, potentially curative therapy (RP (radical prostatectomy) or EBRT) prolonged LE (life expectancy) up to age 75 years but did not improve QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) at any age. For moderately differentiated cancers, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 75 years. For poorly differentiated disease, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 80 years. Benefits of potentially curative therapy were restricted to men with no worse than mild comorbidity. When cohort and pooled case series data were used, RP (radical prostatectomy) was preferred over EBRT in all groups but was comparable to modern radiotherapy.

The study evaluated 629 patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer) who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2010 and 2013. Exclusion criteria were signs of systemic infection, symptoms of an autoimmune disease or neoadjuvant androgen deprivation.

Prior decision-analytic models are based on outdated or suboptimal efficacy, patient preference, and comorbidity data. We estimated life expectancy (LE (life expectancy)) and quality-adjusted life expectancy (QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy)) associated with available treatments for localized prostate cancer in men aged>/= 65 years, adjusting for Gleason score, patient preferences, and comorbidity.

The treatment and outcome of 369 eligible patients with Stage T1-T3aN0-NXM0 prostate cancer were analyzed during a minimal 10-year follow-up period. All patients were treated with curative intent to a mean dose of 65 Gy. The full history of any metastatic disease was documented for each subject, including the initial site of involvement, any progression over time, and patient survival.

The study population included 994 men (4,937 observations) without prostate cancer in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging. Mixed effects models were used to examine the relationship between prostate specific antigen and body mass index in kg/m(2) by age. Separate models were explored in men with prostate cancer censored at diagnosis, for percent body fat measurements, for weight changes with time and adjusting for initial prostate size in 483 men (2,523 observations) with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging measurements.
results.reference: Potentially curative therapy results in significantly improved LE and QALE for older men with few comorbidities and moderately or poorly differentiated localized prostate cancer. Age should not be a barrier to treatment in this group.

results.question: Pituitary apoplexy: do histological features influence the clinical presentation and outcome?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a retrospective analysis of patients with pituitary apoplexy divided into groups based on histological features (infarction alone vs. hemorrhagic infarction/hemorrhage) and compare their clinical presentation and outcomes. This indicates that histological features were considered relevant to clinical presentation and outcome in pituitary apoplexy.

yes
contexts: A retrospective analysis of a contemporary series of patients with pituitary apoplexy was performed to ascertain whether the histopathological features influence the clinical presentation or the outcome.

A retrospective analysis was performed in 59 patients treated for pituitary apoplexy at the University of Virginia Health System, Charlottesville, Virginia, or Groote Schuur Hospital, University of Cape Town, South Africa. The patients were divided into two groups according to the histological features of their disease: one group with infarction alone, comprising 22 patients; and the other with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage, comprising 37 patients. The presenting symptoms, clinical features, endocrinological status, and outcome were compared between the two groups.
To assess the results of transsphenoidal pituitary surgery in patients with Cushing's disease over a period of 18 years, and to determine if there are factors which will predict the outcome.
The characteristics of both tumors, their association with tumors in other sites and the time of presentation are analyzed.

Patients were divided into three groups (remission, failure and relapse) depending on the late outcome of their treatment as determined at the time of analysis, i.e. 88 months (median) years after surgery. Remission is defined as biochemical reversal of hypercortisolism with re-emergence of diurnal circadian rhythm, resolution of clinical features and adequate suppression on low-dose dexamethasone testing. Failure is defined as the absence of any of these features. Relapse is defined as the re-emergence of Cushing's disease more than one year after operation. Clinical features such as weight, sex, hypertension, associated endocrine disorders and smoking, biochemical studies including preoperative and postoperative serum cortisol, urine free cortisol, serum ACTH, radiological, histological and surgical findings were assessed in relation to these three groups to determine whether any factors could reliably predict failure or relapse after treatment.
results.reference: The patients who presented with histological features of pituitary tumor infarction alone had less severe clinical features on presentation, a longer course prior to presentation, and a better outcome than those presenting with hemorrhagic infarction or frank hemorrhage. The endocrine replacement requirements were similar in both groups.

results.question: Do African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that African American women had a higher baseline weight and BMI and consumed slightly more calories than non-African American women during the controlled feeding study. After adjusting for confounders, there was no significant difference in caloric intake required to maintain weight between African American and non-African American women. Therefore, the evidence does not support the idea that African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight.

no
contexts: The high prevalence of obesity in African American (AA (african american)) women may result, in part, from a lower resting metabolic rate (RMR (resting metabolic rate)) than non-AA (african american) women. If true, AA (african american) women should require fewer calories than non-AA (african american) women to maintain weight. Our objective was to determine in the setting of a controlled feeding study, if AA (african american) women required fewer calories than non-AA (african american) women to maintain weight.

AA (african american) women had higher baseline weight and body mass index than non-AA (african american) women (78.4 vs 72.4 kg, P<.01; 29.0 vs 27.6 kg/m(2), P<.05, respectively). During intervention feeding, mean (SD) kcal was 2168 (293) in AA (african american) women and 2073 (284) in non-AA (african american) women. Mean intake was 94.7 kcal higher in AA (african american) women than in non-AA (african american) women (P<.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, there was no difference in caloric intake between AA (african american) and non-AA (african american) women (Δ = -2.8 kcal, P = .95).

This analysis includes 206 women (73% AA (african american)), aged 22-75 years, who participated in the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH (dietary approaches to stop hypertension)) trial-a multicenter, randomized, controlled, feeding study comparing the effects of 3 dietary patterns on blood pressure in individuals with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension. After a 3-week run-in, participants were randomized to 1 of 3 dietary patterns for 8 weeks. Calorie intake was adjusted during feeding to maintain stable weight. The primary outcome of this analysis was average daily calorie (kcal) intake during feeding.

African-American and Hispanic women generally experience higher mortality than White non-Hispanics, and these differences are especially significant in the southeast metropolitan areas and southwest border of Texas. The proportion and location of significant racial disparities however changed depending on the type of statistic (RR (relative risk) versus RD) and the geographic level. The largest proportion of significant results was observed for the RD statistic and census tract data. Geographic regions with significant racial disparities for African-Americans and Hispanics frequently had a poverty rate above 10.00%.

After adjustment for age and race, weight scaled to height in men and women with mean (±SEE) powers of 2.29 ± 0.11 and 1.80 ± 0.07, respectively (both P<0.001). Although univariate circumference-height models were weak or nonsignificant, when adjusted for age and race WC (waist circumference) and HC (hip circumference) scaled to height with powers of 0.76 ± 0.08 and 0.45 ± 0.05, respectively, in men and 0.80 ± 0.05 and 0.53 ± 0.04, respectively, in women (all P<0.001). Age- and race-adjusted incremental increases in circumferences ranged from 0.2 to 0.5 cm per centimeter increase in height. Both WC (waist circumference)/height and HC (hip circumference)/height scaled negatively to height in men and women, and WC (waist circumference)/HC (hip circumference) scaled negatively to height in women only (all P<0.001). Health status-adjusted models were similar.
results.reference: These results do not support the view that AA women are at greater risk for obesity because they require fewer calories to maintain weight.

results.question: Emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy: a feasible combined approach in acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy (CE) was used in patients with overt obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). This combined approach was feasible and influenced management decisions in 25% of patients, suggesting it is a practical and useful strategy in acute settings.

yes
contexts: There are few data concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy)) and its usefulness in the management of severe acute obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate emergency DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy) and capsule endoscopy (CE (capsule endoscopy)) in patients with overt OGIB, analyzing the feasibility of this combined approach.

Emergency DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy) in patients with overt OGIB was defined as performance within 24 h of symptom onset. We reported 27 patients (16 men, mean age: 64.6 ± 17.9 years) with overt severe bleeding who underwent 29 emergency DBE (22 anterograde, 7 retrograde). Of 27 patients, 16 (59.3%) underwent CE (capsule endoscopy) with real time (RT (real time)) viewing.

Patients were diagnosed with the following: Dieulafoy's lesion (DL; n = 11, 40.7%), angioectasia (n = 7, 25.9%), tumors (n = 4, 14.8%), diverticulum (n = 3, 11.1%), ulcers (n = 2, 7.4%). We diagnosed 23 lesions amenable to endoscopic hemostasis and successfully treated 21 of them (77.8%). DL detection rate was statistically higher in the emergency DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy) group than in OGIB patients with DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy) done 24 h after symptom onset (40.7% vs 0.9%, respectively, P < 0.001). Combined approach with RT (real time) viewing by CE (capsule endoscopy) correctly modified DBE (concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy) management in four patients (25%).

From March 2007 to January 2011, 88 DBE procedures were performed on 66 patients. Indications included evaluation anemia/gastrointestinal bleed, small bowel IBD (inflammatory bowel disease) and dilation of strictures. Video-capsule endoscopy (VCE) was used prior to DBE in 43 of the 66 patients prior to DBE evaluation.

We have previously reported the feasibility of diagnostic and therapeutic peritoneoscopy including liver biopsy, gastrojejunostomy, and tubal ligation by an oral transgastric approach. We present results of per-oral transgastric splenectomy in a porcine model. The goal of this study was to determine the technical feasibility of per-oral transgastric splenectomy using a flexible endoscope.
results.reference: Emergency DBE is feasible, safe and effective in acute OGIB and may avoid major surgery, diagnosing and successfully treating most patients. Combined approach with RT viewing by CE is especially useful to identify recurrent bleeding vascular lesions such as DL that may be easily misdiagnosed by non-emergency DBE.

results.question: Cardiopulmonary bypass temperature does not affect postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome?
results.answer:
The first abstract specifically aims to determine if temperature during cardiopulmonary bypass affects perioperative and postoperative thyroid function, which is related to euthyroid sick syndrome. However, none of the provided abstracts report the results or conclusions of this study, so there is no direct evidence here to confirm or refute the effect of CPB temperature on postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome.

maybe
contexts: To determine if temperature during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) has an effect on perioperative and postoperative thyroid function.

This prospective randomized study was carried out with 100 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass operations between April 1999 and November 2000 in Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Patients were divided into 2 groups. Desmopressin (0.3 microg/kg) was administrated just after cardiopulmonary bypass and after protamine infusion in group 1 (n = 50). Both desmopressin and tranexamic acid (before the skin incision at a loading dose of 10 mg/kg over 30 minutes and followed by 12 hours of 1 mg.kg(-1).h(-1)) were administrated in group 2 (n = 50).

Patients who underwent an appendectomy at the Ren-Ai branch of Taipei City Hospital between January 2010 and October 2012 were retrospectively reviewed. Their demographics, white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, body temperature, computed tomography scan usage, operation method, pathology report, postoperative complication, length of hospital stay, and ETA were abstracted. Multivariate analysis was performed to search the predictors, including ETA, of outcomes for the perforation and postoperative complication rates.

Desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which augments cardiopulmonary bypass--associated hyperfibrinolysis, causing excessive bleeding. Combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of the antifibrinolytic drug tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and might improve postoperative hemostasis.

Patients with SCD (sickle cell disease) presenting to the emergency department and hematology clinic with temperature greater than or equal to 38 degrees C were prospectively evaluated using a physician-completed questionnaire. The questionnaire included inquiries into the patient's physical signs and symptoms and the physician's clinical impression for the presence of ACS. The questionnaire was completed before obtaining CXR results in all patients.
results.reference: The results of this study suggest that normothermic CPB does not prevent the development of the "euthyroid sick syndrome" during and after CPB. Despite these changes in thyroid function, most patients in both groups had a normal postoperative recovery.

results.question: Body dysmorphic disorder: does it have a psychotic subtype?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) can present with psychotic features, as there is a distinction made between nonpsychotic BDD (with some insight) and psychotic BDD (without insight and of delusional intensity). The study comparing these subtypes found differences in psychotic disorder diagnoses, supporting the existence of a psychotic subtype of BDD.

yes
contexts: Although body dysmorphic disorder (BDD (body dysmorphic disorder)) is classified in DSM-III-R as a nonpsychotic somatoform disorder, controversy exists as to whether BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) can present with psychotic features. If it can, this raises the possibility that its DSM-III-R psychotic counterpart-delusional disorder, somatic type--may not be a separate disorder. The purpose of this study was to determine whether patients with nonpsychotic BDD (defined according to DSM-III-R criteria, i.e., with maintenance of some insight) were different from patients with psychotic BDD (those whose preoccupation was without insight and of delusional intensity).

Patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) displayed a significantly higher rate of lifetime DSM-III-R psychotic disorder diagnoses than patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder). However, the two groups did not differ significantly on most other variables examined. For instance, both psychotic and nonpsychotic patients displayed significant morbidity; high comorbidity with mood, anxiety, and psychoactive substance use disorders; and apparent preferential response to serotonin reuptake inhibitors rather than to non-serotonin reuptake blocking antidepressants or antipsychotics.

Fifty consecutive patients meeting DSM-III-R criteria A and C for BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were assessed with a semistructured interview and the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R (SCID (structured clinical interview for dsm-iii-r)). Family histories of psychiatric disorders were blindly assessed. The 24 patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were compared with the 26 patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) with respect to demographics, phenomenology, course of illness, associated features, comorbid psychiatric disorders, family history, and treatment response.

Women's vulnerability for a first lifetime-onset of major depressive disorder (MDD (major depressive disorder)) during midlife is substantial. It is unclear whether risk factors differ for first lifetime-onset and recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder). Identifying these risk factors can provide more focused depression screening and earlier intervention. This study aims to evaluate whether lifetime psychiatric and health histories, personality traits, menopausal status and factors that vary over time, e.g. symptoms, are independent risk factors for first-onset or recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder) across 13 annual follow-ups.

This was a retrospective study of 18 consecutive adults with a partial seizure disorder and PIPE (study group) and 36 patients with a partial seizure disorder but without PIPE (control group). These two groups were compared with respect to the likelihood of developing IPE (interictal psychotic episodes) over an 8-year follow-up period and the variables operant in the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Statistical analyses consisted of logistic regression models to identify the variables predictive of the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Predictors included: number and location of ictal foci, seizure type, etiology, age at seizure onset, duration of seizure disorder, MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) abnormalities, and psychiatric history prior to the index video/EEG (electroencephalogram) monitoring (other than PIPE).
results.reference: Body dysmorphic disorder may have a closely related psychotic subtype that significantly overlaps with, or may even be the same disorder as, the BDD variant of delusional disorder, somatic type. Inclusion of a psychotic subtype for BDD should be considered for future editions of DSM.

results.question: Does receipt of hospice care in nursing homes improve the management of pain at the end of life?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that hospice residents in nursing homes are more likely to receive regular treatment for daily pain compared to nonhospice residents, with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.08. Additionally, hospice residents were less likely to receive no analgesics and less likely to receive analgesics not recommended by guidelines, suggesting better adherence to pain management standards. Therefore, hospice care appears to improve pain management at the end of life in nursing homes.

yes
contexts: A subset of residents with daily pain near the end of life taken from a matched cohort of hospice (2,644) and nonhospice (7,929) nursing home residents who had at least two resident assessments (Minimum Data Sets (MDSs)) completed, their last between 1992 and 1996, and who died before April 1997. The daily pain subset consisted of 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents.
To compare analgesic management of daily pain for dying nursing home residents enrolled and not enrolled in Medicare hospice.

Fifteen percent of hospice residents and 23% of nonhospice residents in daily pain received no analgesics (odds ratio (OR (odds ratio)) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)) = 0.45-0.74). A lower proportion of hospice residents (21%) than of nonhospice residents (29%) received analgesics not recommended by AMDA (OR (odds ratio) = 0.65, 95% CI (confidence interval) =0.52-0.80). Overall, acetaminophen (not in combination with other drugs) was used most frequently for nonhospice residents (25% of 1,673 prescriptions), whereas morphine derivatives were used most frequently for hospice residents (30% of 1,058 prescriptions). Fifty-one percent of hospice residents and 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain. Controlling for clinical confounders, hospice residents were twice as likely as nonhospice residents to receive regular treatment for daily pain (adjusted odds ratio = 2.08, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.68-2.56).

Detailed drug use data contained on the last MDS before death were used to examine analgesic management of daily pain. Guidelines from the American Medical Directors Association (AMDA (american medical directors association)) were used to identify analgesics not recommended for use in managing chronic pain in long-term care settings. The study outcome, regular treatment of daily pain, examined whether patients received any analgesic, other than those not recommended by AMDA (american medical directors association), at least twice a day for each day of documented daily pain (i.e., 7 days before date of last MDS).

A secondary analysis of one-hundred-sixty-seven patients referred for treatment of cancer-related pain was conducted. Pain intensity at admission was recorded and patients were divided in three categories of pain intensity: mild, moderate and severe. Patients were offered a treatment with opioid dose titration, according to department policy. Data regarding opioid doses and pain intensity were collected after dose titration was completed. Four levels of opioid response were considered: (a) good pain control, with minimal opioid escalation and without relevant adverse effects; (b) good pain control requiring more aggressive opioid escalation, for example doubling the doses in four days; (c) adequate pain control associated with the occurrence of adverse effects; (d) poor pain control with adverse effects.
results.reference: Findings suggest that analgesic management of daily pain is better for nursing home residents enrolled in hospice than for those not enrolled in hospice.The prescribing practices portrayed by this study reveal that many dying nursing home residents in daily pain are receiving no analgesic treatment or are receiving analgesic treatment inconsistent with AMDA and other pain management guidelines. Improving the analgesic management of pain in nursing homes is essential if high-quality end-of-life care in nursing homes is to be achieved.

results.question: Fulfilling human resources development goal in West Africa: can the training of ophthalmologist diplomates be improved?
results.answer:
The context includes a study aimed at ascertaining the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training in West Africa with a view to improving the program. yes
contexts: To ascertain the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats (TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats)) on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training (ODT (ophthalmic diploma training)) in West Africa with a view to improving the programme.
A survey of set 2005 TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats) on ODT (ophthalmic diploma training) was carried out in Ghana, 2006.

Longitudinal cohort studies in sub-Saharan Africa are urgently needed to understand cardiovascular disease development. As with some procedures, trauma fellowship training and greater surgeon experience may result in better outcomes following intramedullary nailing (IMN) of diaphyseal femur fractures. However, surgeons with such training and experience may not always be available to all patients. The purpose of this study is to determine whether trauma training affects the post-operative difference in femoral version (DFV (difference in femoral version)) following IMN.

The Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology study in the North West Province, South Africa, started in 2005 and included African volunteers (n = 1994; aged>30 years) from a sample of 6000 randomly selected households in rural and urban areas.
results.reference: The ODT programme ensures ophthalmic manpower for secondary eye care level despite challenges. The stakeholders should look into problems facing the programme in order to improve it.

results.question: Does binge drinking during early pregnancy increase the risk of psychomotor deficits?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that there were no significant differences in motor function at age 5 between children of mothers who reported isolated binge drinking episodes during early pregnancy and those who did not binge drink. Additionally, no association was found with the number or timing of binge episodes. Therefore, the evidence does not support an increased risk of psychomotor deficits due to binge drinking in early pregnancy.

no
contexts: The potential effects of binge drinking during pregnancy on child motor function have only been assessed in a few, small studies. We aimed to examine the effects of binge alcohol consumption during early pregnancy, including number of binge episodes and timing of binge drinking, on child motor function at age 5.

There were no systematic or significant differences in motor function between children of mothers reporting isolated episodes of binge drinking and children of mothers with no binge episodes. No association was observed with respect to the number of binge episodes (maximum of 12) and timing of binge drinking.
To explore the long-term (10-year) transmission of familial drinking during adolescence to offspring drinking patterns in young adulthood.

That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.

To investigate if fetal gender (1) affects the risk of having an emergency department (ED (emergency department)) visit for asthma; and (2) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had at least one visit to the ED (emergency department) for asthma during pregnancy.
results.reference: In this study, we found no systematic association between isolated episodes of binge drinking during early pregnancy and child motor function at age 5.

results.question: Does tranexamic acid reduce desmopressin-induced hyperfibrinolysis?
results.answer:
The first abstract states that desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which increases hyperfibrinolysis and causes excessive bleeding. It also suggests that combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and improve postoperative hemostasis. The second abstract describes a study where tranexamic acid was given before surgery along with desmopressin, implying that tranexamic acid can counteract the hyperfibrinolytic effect induced by desmopressin.

yes
contexts: Desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which augments cardiopulmonary bypass--associated hyperfibrinolysis, causing excessive bleeding. Combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of the antifibrinolytic drug tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and might improve postoperative hemostasis.

This prospective randomized study was carried out with 100 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass operations between April 1999 and November 2000 in Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Patients were divided into 2 groups. Desmopressin (0.3 microg/kg) was administrated just after cardiopulmonary bypass and after protamine infusion in group 1 (n = 50). Both desmopressin and tranexamic acid (before the skin incision at a loading dose of 10 mg/kg over 30 minutes and followed by 12 hours of 1 mg.kg(-1).h(-1)) were administrated in group 2 (n = 50).

It is postulated that some aspects of methotrexate toxicity may be related to its action as an anti-folate. Folic acid (FA (folic acid)) is often given as an adjunct to methotrexate therapy, but there is no conclusive proof that it decreases the toxicity of methotrexate and there is a theoretical risk that it may decrease the efficacy of methotrexate.

To look at the effect of stopping FA (folic acid) supplementation in UK rheumatoid arthritis (RA (rheumatoid arthritis)) patients established on methotrexate<20 mg weekly and FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily, to report all toxicity (including absolute changes in haematological and liver enzyme indices) and to report changes in the efficacy of methotrexate.

In a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 75 patients who were established on methotrexate<20 mg weekly and FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily were asked to stop their FA (folic acid) and were randomized to one of two groups: placebo or FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily. results.question: Does ultrasound-scored synovitis depend on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1], [2], and [5] investigated ultrasound-detected synovitis in RA patients treated with subcutaneous anti-TNF agents at both peak and trough plasma drug concentrations. The results showed no significant differences in ultrasound parameters of synovitis between peak and trough times, indicating that synovitis scores do not vary with the pharmacokinetics of the drug. Therefore, ultrasound-scored synovitis does not depend on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents in these patients.

no
contexts: The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of the pharmacokinetics of s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents on the grade of US (ultrasound)-detected synovitis in RA patients.

Fifty RA patients were prospectively recruited from the Biologic Therapy Unit of our hospital. Inclusion criteria were being in treatment with s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents and having had neither changes in therapy nor local corticosteroid injections in the previous 3 months. Patients underwent clinical, laboratory [28-joint DAS (DAS28) and Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI (simplified disease activity index))]and US (ultrasound) assessment at two time points, i.e. at peak plasma drug concentration and at trough plasma drug concentration. US (ultrasound) assessments were performed blindly to the anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agent, the administration time and the clinical and laboratory data. Twenty-eight joints were investigated for the presence and grade (0-3) of B-mode synovitis and synovial power Doppler signal. Global indices for B-mode synovitis (BSI) and Doppler synovitis (DSI) were calculated for 12 joints and for wrist-hand-ankle-foot joints. B-mode US (ultrasound) remission was defined as a BSI<1 and Doppler US (ultrasound) remission as a DSI<1.

results.question: Counter sampling combined with medical provider education: do they alter prescribing behavior?
results.answer:

contexts: To observe if medical providers alter their prescribing patterns of three relatively expensive categories of medications provided as samples by manufacturers (focus medications) when they receive additional education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower cost alternatives (counter samples) that are made available to dispense.

The prescribing behavior of medical providers in the active intervention and control groups were significantly different at baseline in all three categories of focus medications. Medical providers in the intervention group significantly decreased the use of COX-2 NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions relative to total NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions following active intervention (38.9% in year 1 versus 23.7% in year 2, P<0.05). Over the same two time periods, a nonstatistically significant decrease in COX-2 NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescribing was seen at the control site (67.5% versus 62%, P>0.05). Education and counter sampling did not stop medical providers from significantly increasing the total yearly prescriptions for antihistamines and acid-relief medications that consisted of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (86.7% versus 93.1%, P<0.05) and PPIs (68.9% versus 86.2%, P<0.05). Statistically significant increases in the prescribing of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (77.9% versus 98.3%, P<0.05) and PPIs (77.5% versus 91.4%, P<0.05) were also observed in the control group.

results.question: Failed IUD insertions in community practice: an under-recognized problem?
results.answer:
The data from the provided abstracts indicate that there is a notable rate of unsuccessful IUD insertions in community practice settings, particularly among nulliparous women, with failure rates of 19.6% and 13.6% in nulliparous and parous women respectively. The adjusted odds ratio suggests a higher likelihood of failure in nulliparous women, and the study setting involved nurse practitioners in community clinics without additional facilitative measures, highlighting that failed IUD insertions may indeed be an under-recognized problem in such settings.

yes
contexts: Six providers performed 197 IUD insertion attempts. These providers had a mean of 14.1 years of experience (range 1-27, S.D. ±12.5). Among nulliparous women, 27 of 138 (19.6%) IUD insertions were unsuccessful. In parous women, 8 of 59 IUD insertions were unsuccessful (13.6%). Adjuvant measures to facilitate difficult IUD insertions (cervical anesthesia, dilation, pain medication, and use of ultrasound guidance) were not utilized. No differences before or after the PEP (perinatal education programme) were detected. Where problems were detected, appropriate actions taken during labour improved, but not significantly.

results.question: Type II supracondylar humerus fractures: can some be treated nonoperatively?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that some type II supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFs) can indeed be treated nonoperatively. Specifically, 57.9% of fractures in one study were successfully managed without surgery, especially those without rotational deformity or coronal angulation and with a shaft-condylar angle >15 degrees. contexts: The range of injury severity that can be seen within the category of type II supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFs) raises the question whether some could be treated nonoperatively. Ultimately, 150 fractures (57.9%) were treated nonoperatively, and 109 fractures (42.1%) were treated surgically. At final follow-up, outcome measures of change in carrying angle, range of motion, and complications did not show clinically significant differences between treatment groups. Fractures without rotational deformity or coronal angulation and with a shaft-condylar angle of>15 degrees were more likely to be associated with successful nonsurgical treatment. A scoring system was developed using these features to stratify the severity of the injury. Patients with isolated extension deformity, but none of the other features, were more likely to complete successful nonoperative management.

results.reference: This study suggests that some of the less severe pediatric type II SCHFs can be successfully treated without surgery if close follow-up is achieved. results.question: The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: are they worth the price?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that specialty pharmaceuticals offer significant benefits such as increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, and reduced disease burden, which suggest they provide value despite their high cost. However, the high expense and need for careful management and evidence of value complicate their cost-effectiveness assessment. Overall, the promise of specialty pharmaceuticals appears to justify their price when managed appropriately.

yes
contexts: The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, enhanced workplace productivity, decreased burden of disease, and reduced health care spending comes at a significant cost. These agents require special handling, administration, patient education, clinical support, and risk mitigation. Additionally, specialty drugs require distribution systems that ensure appropriate patient selection and data collection. With the specialty pharmaceutical pipeline overflowing with new medicines and an aging population increasingly relying on these novel treatments to treat common diseases, the challenge of managing the costs associated with these agents can be daunting. Aided by sophisticated pharmacoeconomic models to assess value, the cost impacts of these specialty drugs can be appropriately controlled.
To outline emerging strategies and case study examples for the medical and pharmacy benefits management of specialty pharmaceuticals.

Determining the value of these medications is hampered by a lack of robust pharmacoeconomic data.

results.question: Does invasive diagnosis of nosocomial pneumonia during off-hours delay treatment?

results.question: Undescended testes: does age at orchiopexy affect survival of the testis?
results.answer:

results.question: Do lipids, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking confer equal risk of myocardial infarction in women as in men?
results.answer:

results.question: Does family practice at residency teaching sites reflect community practice?

results.question: Midwives' competence: is it affected by working in a rural location?
results.answer:

results.question: Evaluation of pediatric VCUG at an academic children's hospital: is the radiographic scout image necessary?

contexts: There is heterogeneity in how pediatric voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) is performed. Some institutions, including our own, obtain a radiographic scout image prior to contrast agent instillation.
To demonstrate that the radiographic scout image does not augment VCUG interpretation or contribute management-changing information but nonetheless carries a non-negligible effective dose.

We evaluated 181 children who underwent VCUG in 2012, with an age breakdown of less than 1 year (56 children), 1-5 years (66 children), 6-10 years (43 children) and 11-18 years (16 children), with a mean age of 4.0 years. We investigated patient demographics, clinical indication for the examination, scout image findings and estimated effective radiation dose, as well as overall exam findings and impression.

No clinically significant or management-changing findings were present on scout images, and no radiopaque urinary tract calculi or concerning incidental finding was identified. Scout image estimated effective radiation dose averaged 0.09 mSv in children younger than 1 y, 0.09 mSv in children age 1-5, 0.13 mSv in children age 6-10 and 0.18 mSv in children age 11-18. Total fluoroscopy time per examination averaged 36.7 s (range 34.8-39.6 s for all age group averages). Evaluation of known or suspected vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) and urinary tract infection (UTI (urinary tract infection)) were the most common clinical indications, stated in 40.9% and 37.0% of exams, respectively.

We reviewed clinical and radiographic information on 259 pediatric type II SCHFs that were enrolled in a prospective registry of elbow fractures. The characteristics of the patients who were treated without surgery were compared with those of patients who were treated surgically. Treatment outcomes, as assessed by the final clinical and radiographic alignment, range of motion of the elbow, and complications, were compared between the groups to define clinical and radiographic features that related to success or failure of nonoperative management.
results.reference: Although the estimated effective dose is low for VCUG radiographic scout images, this step did not augment VCUG interpretation or contribute management-changing information. This step should be omitted or substituted to further reduce dose in pediatric VCUG.

results.question: Are endometrial polyps from pre-menopausal women similar to post-menopausal women?
results.answer:
Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women show significant differences in the expression of hormone receptors and Ki67, indicating they are not similar in these aspects. However, both groups have similarly increased levels of Bcl-2. Overall, the differences in key markers suggest they are not similar.

no
contexts: Do endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women have similar immunohistochemical expression of oestrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) and markers of cellular proliferation/apoptosis (Ki67 and Bcl-2).
Fourteen pre-menopausal and 16 post-menopausal women who presented with abnormal bleeding with endometrial polyps.

Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women had significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67. However, polyps from both groups of women had similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, an inhibitor of apoptosis.
Polyps recruited from women attending an out-patient hysteroscopy clinic in a UK district general hospital.
Immunohistochemical staining was performed on endometrial polyps.
results.reference: Pre- and post-menopausal polyps exhibit differing hormone receptor and proliferation markers, presumably a result of their hormonal milieu. However, both groups appear to have lost the usual control mechanisms for apoptotic regulation, this appears to be responsible for their growth.

results.question: Does accompanying metabolic syndrome contribute to heart dimensions in hypertensive patients?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that hypertensive patients with metabolic syndrome (MetS) have significantly greater left atrial diameter compared to those without MetS, and this diameter correlates with the number of MetS criteria. While other heart dimensions are increased in hypertensive patients regardless of MetS, the presence of MetS specifically contributes to changes in left atrial size.

yes
contexts: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events. We evaluated heart dimensions in hypertensive patients with MetS.

Metabolic syndrome was present in 32 hypertensive patients (42.7%; 18 males, 14 females). The mean number of MetS criteria was 2.6+/-1.0 in the hypertensive group. Compared to the control group, patients with or without MetS exhibited significantly increased interventricular septum and posterior wall thickness, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass (p<0.05). The only significant difference between the two patient groups was that MetS was associated with a greater left atrial diameter (p=0.019). Left atrial diameter was correlated with the number of MetS criteria (r=0.51; p<0.001).
To determine whether anginal episodes might be related to extremes of hypotension in patients with ischaemic heart disease taking drugs to treat angina and heart failure.

Hypertension is one of the important contributing factors linked with both causation and development of kidney disease. It is a multifactorial, polygenic, and complex disorder due to interaction of several risk genes with environmental factors. The present study was aimed to explore genetic polymorphism in ACE-1 gene as a risk factor for CKD (chronic kidney disease) among hypertensive patients.

LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) was present in 42 patients (42%) of the study group, none among controls. Hypertensive patients had significantly greater indices of LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) and QTcD compared with controls (p<0.001 for all). Similarly, among hypertensive patients, those with LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) had a significantly greater QTcD compared with those without (p<0.001). Pearson's correlation coefficient test demonstrated strongly positive correlations between QTcD and the indices of LVH (p<0.001 for all). Analysis of the receiver operating characteristic curves identified 60 ms as the optimal cut-off value of QTcD that best predicts LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) in hypertensives. Using this value, QTcD was able to predict LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) with a sensitivity of 92.9% and specificity 98.2%.
results.reference: Left ventricular dimensions are not influenced by MetS. Rather than MetS, hypertension is primarily responsible for changes in left ventricular dimensions. However, left atrial enlargement is more prominent in patients with MetS, suggesting that each MetS criterion contributes to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction.

results.question: The Prevalence of Incidentally Detected Idiopathic Misty Mesentery on Multidetector Computed Tomography: Can Obesity Be the Triggering Cause?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that among patients with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on CT, a high proportion were classified as obese (67.5%) or overweight (17.5%). This suggests a possible association between obesity and the presence of idiopathic misty mesentery, implying that obesity could be a triggering factor. Therefore, the evidence supports the hypothesis that obesity may be related to the prevalence of idiopathic misty mesentery.

yes
contexts: Misty mesentery appearance is commonly reported in daily practice, usually as a secondary finding of various pathological entities, but sometimes it is encountered as an isolated finding that cannot be attributed to any other disease entity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of cases with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and to summarize the pathologies leading to this appearance.

There were a total of 561 patients in whom misty mesentery appearance was depicted on abdominopelvic CT (computed tomography) scans. A total of 80 cases were found to have isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7%. The common indication for CT (computed tomography) examination was abdominal pain. There was a slight female predominance (51.3%). 67.5% of all patients were classified as obese and 17.5% as overweight.
